welcome.label: Welcome · the canal hum

parts.label: 🔊 Today
parts.title: What is sound, really?
parts.body: Vibrations, waves, and high and low pitch.

welcome.script:
(Put your fingers on your throat and hum.) Mmmmm. Feel that buzz?

[ON SCREEN: The front page]
Now imagine a hum like that coming through your bedroom walls every night, and nobody knows where it comes from.

[ON SCREEN: Today]
Today you’ll find out what sound really is. Read the front page in the case file just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · hold it to stop it (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Tap a glass with a spoon, then touch it.) Ding… and gone. My finger stopped something.

[ON SCREEN: Make it ring]
What was the glass doing while it rang?

[ON SCREEN: Hold it to stop it]
Make each one ring, then press and hold the picture to stop it. Press Listen on Sam’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

part1.label: Part 1 · be the vibration (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Stand in a line with stuffed animals, and bump the first one.) Bump, bump, bump. The push moved down the line. Did any of them walk to the end?

[ON SCREEN: Be the vibration]
That’s how sound travels. Wiggle the tuning fork and keep your eye on the red dot. Press Listen.

part2.label: Part 2 · match the note (Clue 3)
part2.script:
(Stretch a rubber band and pluck it, then pull it tighter and pluck again.) Hear the difference?

[ON SCREEN: Match the note]
Tune the band by ear to match three notes. Then pluck it hard. Does it get higher, or just louder?

explore.label: Part 3 · the ruler test (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Hold a ruler on the edge of a table and twang it.) Bwoing!

[ON SCREEN: The ruler test]
Your turn. Change only ONE thing: how much ruler hangs off. Listen to each length, and the table fills in. If you have a ruler, try it for real, too! Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What is making the hum?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Four clues: crack the case at the top of this tab.

[ON SCREEN: The hum-maker]
Then meet the real hum-maker, and write back to the newspaper.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Last, two short answers, your sound model with a labeled sketch, and your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Sound is something invisible that flies through the air, like a tiny ball.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A tiny ball? Hmm. Think about that red dot. Where did it go?

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts, then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🎧 Your specimen
parts.title: The canal hum recording
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Moving air and water
parts.body: Can wind and water do work?

closing.script:
(Cup a hand behind your ear.) Shhh. Hear that? Fish, drumming in a canal!

[ON SCREEN: Bonus: the hydrophone]
Want to listen underwater? Try the hydrophone at the very end.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and the canal hum recording goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time: can moving air and water do work? Bring a pinwheel if you have one!

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
